name: load_audio_channel_tables
description: Writes start address, length and period values into the four audio channel register blocks, builds a chain of pointer fields from a table, and calls a setup routine three times before returning. The facts show no separate callers beyond the one unnamed routine.

name: reload_audio_channel_setup
description: Repeats the table-driven audio channel setup with the same register writes and three setup calls, then returns its input values unchanged. It is a near copy of the routine that performs the initial audio setup.

name: reset_record_fields_to_defaults
description: Clears a block of fields in the record addressed by the first address register, copies one value from a second record into a field, and sets one byte to a fixed count. The routine has only two instructions of control flow and makes no calls.

name: write_control_word_clear_bit
description: Writes two values to a global control variable, then clears its second bit. The facts list the joystick and fire-button port, DMA control and interrupt enable registers as touched by this routine.

name: examine_undecoded_eight_instruction_routine
description: No pseudo-code could be recovered, so the body is unknown. The facts show eight instructions, one unnamed caller, and that it is entered as a called routine that is also executed in the reference run.

key: indiana jones and the fate of atlantis - arcade (1992)(lucasarts)[cr csl][t supplex]/Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis - Arcade (1992)(LucasArts)[cr CSL][t Supplex].adf:SUPPLEX:0:0000
name: write_colour_registers_on_entry
description: Program entry point that writes to the colour register bank and calls four other routines. Pseudo-code could not be recovered, so only the register use, call count and caller count are known.

key: indiana jones and the fate of atlantis - arcade (1992)(lucasarts)[cr csl][t supplex]/Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis - Arcade (1992)(LucasArts)[cr CSL][t Supplex].adf:SUPPLEX:0:0070
name: refill_bit_buffer_word
description: Loads the 32-bit word that precedes the source pointer, clears a 16-bit location through the second pointer, and returns that word shifted right by one bit with the top bit set. This is a bit-buffer refill used by a decoder.

key: indiana jones and the fate of atlantis - arcade (1992)(lucasarts)[cr csl][t supplex]/Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis - Arcade (1992)(LucasArts)[cr CSL][t Supplex].adf:SUPPLEX:0:0096
name: discard_bits_from_stream
description: Shifts out as many bits as its input count from a bit buffer, calling the refill routine whenever the buffer word becomes empty.

key: indiana jones and the fate of atlantis - arcade (1992)(lucasarts)[cr csl][t supplex]/Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis - Arcade (1992)(LucasArts)[cr CSL][t Supplex].adf:Indy IV/Indy-IV:0:0000
name: load_hunks_and_apply_relocations
description: Parses AmigaDOS hunk records of a loaded executable. It allocates memory for code, data and BSS hunks through the exec allocator, applies 32-bit relocation fixups, and frees memory on the discard path before finishing as the program entry point.

key: indiana jones and the fate of atlantis - arcade (1992)(lucasarts)[cr csl][t supplex]/Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis - Arcade (1992)(LucasArts)[cr CSL][t Supplex].adf:Indy IV/Indy-IV:0:017C
name: busy_wait_16bit_count
description: Burns time in a software delay by decrementing a 16-bit count until it wraps past zero. The facts also list two library function-table calls for this routine.

key: indiana jones and the fate of atlantis - arcade (1992)(lucasarts)[cr csl][t supplex]/Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis - Arcade (1992)(LucasArts)[cr CSL][t Supplex].adf:Indy IV/Indy-IV:0:01CC
name: decode_compressed_stream_run
description: Decompresses data by reading variable-length codes through a bit reader and copying runs backwards from already written output into the destination, stopping when the destination pointer reaches its start. It calls a bit-buffer check and three other routines.

key: indiana jones and the fate of atlantis - arcade (1992)(lucasarts)[cr csl][t supplex]/Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis - Arcade (1992)(LucasArts)[cr CSL][t Supplex].adf:Indy IV/Indy-IV:0:0218
name: read_bit_sequence_into_word
description: Reads a run of bits from a bit buffer, refilling the buffer word from memory when it empties, and assembles them into an accumulator by shifting each new bit in at the low end. It returns the completed value through the accumulator register.

key: indiana jones and the fate of atlantis - arcade (1992)(lucasarts)[cr csl][t supplex]/Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis - Arcade (1992)(LucasArts)[cr CSL][t Supplex].adf:Indy IV/Indy-IV:0:026C
name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decoded bytes are not valid instructions: a trap is followed by a single byte store and then bad data. The routine is only referenced by address and is not usable code.

name: open_libraries_and_wait_messages
description: Opens and closes exec libraries, locates the current task and waits on its message port. It also writes a copper list pointer and DMA control bits, using the listed exec calls and hardware registers.

name: open_library_install_copper_list
description: Opens library resources under Forbid and Permit, installs a copper list pointer and enables DMA bits, then walks a table of pointers calling a setup routine for each entry. It ends in an endless loop when setup fails.

name: stub_self_assign_and_return
description: Stores a global variable back into itself and returns, so it performs no work. It is reached only because gap bytes decode as code.

name: load_and_unpack_compressed_file
description: Reads from a file through library calls, checking each result for failure. It writes two decimal digits into a text buffer, then expands an LZ-style stream by copying literal bytes and back-references into memory, and drives a CIA port register with short delay loops between steps.

name: read_four_bit_field
description: Reads a 4-bit field from a bit stream at the current bit position, refilling the stream word first when the bit counter is below seven. It then reduces the bit counter by an amount computed from the field width.

name: read_five_bit_field
description: Reads a 5-bit field from a bit stream at the current bit position, refilling the stream word first when the bit counter is below seven. It then reduces the bit counter by an amount computed from the field width.

name: read_six_bit_field
description: Reads a 6-bit field from a bit stream at the current bit position, refilling the stream word first when the bit counter is below seven. It then reduces the bit counter by an amount computed from the field width.

name: read_seven_bit_field
description: Reads a 7-bit field from a bit stream at the current bit position, refilling the stream word first when the bit counter is below seven. It then reduces the bit counter by an amount computed from the field width.

name: read_eight_bit_field
description: Reads an 8-bit field from a bit stream at the current bit position, refilling the stream word first when the bit counter is below seven. It then reduces the bit counter by an amount computed from the field width.

name: read_nine_bit_field
description: Reads a 9-bit field from a bit stream at the current bit position, refilling the stream word first when the bit counter is below seven. It then reduces the bit counter by an amount computed from the field width.

name: copy_block_then_read_file
description: Copies a source block into a destination buffer, clamping the length to a fixed maximum, then calls a library read routine. On a failed read it formats two decimal digits into a message buffer and takes an error path; otherwise it returns the byte count.

name: close_file_handle_if_open
description: Closes the open file handle through the library close call when one is held, then marks the handle as closed with a sentinel value. It does nothing when no handle is open.

name: pulse_cia_port_with_delays
description: Runs two short delay loops, writes a masked pattern to a CIA B port register, runs another delay loop and returns. The register write is the only hardware access shown.

name: allocate_signal_and_init_table
description: Allocates an exec signal bit and finds the current task. On success it clears a small table, stores the signal number and task pointer into control fields and clears a second table; on failure it takes an error path that can end in an endless loop.

name: fill_bytes_with_value
description: Writes one byte value to memory repeatedly for a count given in a data register, advancing the destination pointer by one byte each time.

name: copy_block_forward_or_backward
description: Copies a byte block from source to destination, copying forward when the destination lies below the source and backward otherwise, so overlapping regions are copied correctly.

name: copy_bytes_backward_by_count
description: Copies a block backward from the high end of the source and destination for a given count. The facts also list exec calls for freeing memory, replying to a message and supervisor mode, and writes to the background colour register, copper pointer and DMA control.

name: jump_through_dispatch_table
description: Jumps to one of several routines chosen by a global value through a table, and returns when that routine returns. The table could not be recovered, so the targets are not named.

name: allocate_and_link_list_node
description: Allocates a memory node through the exec allocator, and on success links it into a list by storing two pointer fields and zeroing two others. On failure it calls an error routine and then either runs a recovery path or ends in an endless loop.

name: allocate_node_or_report_error
description: Allocates a memory node through the exec allocator and links it into a list on success. On failure it reports an out-of-memory error text and then takes a recovery path or ends in an endless loop.

name: concatenate_two_strings_into_buffer
description: Copies one zero-terminated string into a fixed buffer, appends a second zero-terminated string after it, and passes the buffer to a library routine. On failure it enters an error path that can end in an endless loop.

name: clear_longword_table_reset_counter
description: Zeroes a fixed table of 32-bit words and then resets a global counter to zero twice. It has no calls and no hardware access.

name: bump_counter_around_two_calls
description: Increments a global counter, calls a routine, resets the counter to zero and calls another routine. The counter is the only state it changes.

name: accumulate_mouse_port_movement
description: Reads the mouse-port movement register twice. For each reading it keeps the low and high byte as current values and adds the change since the last sample into two accumulator words.

name: enable_interrupt_bits
description: Calls two routines, copies a global value through a temporary, and writes an interrupt-enable value with the set-on-write bit to the interrupt enable register. The facts list three calls.

name: read_interrupt_request_state
description: Reads the interrupt enable and interrupt request state registers, with two calls around the reads. No pseudo-code could be recovered, so the rest of the behaviour is not known from the evidence.

name: touch_interrupt_request_register
description: Touches the interrupt request register and makes one call. No pseudo-code could be recovered, so the behaviour is known only from the register use and the instruction count.

name: examine_two_instruction_stub
description: No pseudo-code could be recovered. The facts show two instructions and one unnamed caller, so this is a very short stub whose purpose the evidence does not show.

name: decode_keyboard_serial_byte
description: Reads a byte from a CIA serial data register, inverts and rotates it into a key code, and updates a per-key state table according to the key-down or key-up bit. It then performs the keyboard handshake by writing a control register and waiting on a status bit.

name: store_key_state_and_wait
description: Stores the low seven bits of a key code, saves the previous state of that key's entry and sets the entry from the press or release bit. It waits for a handshake status bit before clearing two control bits; the routine indexes a key-character string only through the key code.

name: enable_interrupts_after_two_calls
description: Calls two routines and then writes a fixed interrupt-enable value to a global. The facts list the two calls and no direct hardware access.

name: disable_interrupts_master_bit
description: Writes a fixed value with the set-or-clear bit clear to the interrupt enable register, which disables the bit it names. Three unnamed routines call it.

name: enable_interrupts_master_bit
description: Writes a fixed value with the set-or-clear bit set to the interrupt enable register, which enables the bit it names. Three unnamed routines call it.

name: setup_interrupt_server_node
description: Clears a small interrupt-server structure, stores a code address and a priority value in it, then opens a system resource. If the resource is found it calls two library functions on it.

name: release_stored_resource_handle
description: If a stored resource handle is set, calls two library functions on it. It is the second half of the setup routine that stores the handle.

name: wait_forever_after_calls
description: Calls two routines and then spins in an endless loop, so it never returns.

name: stub_return_without_work
description: The decompiled body is a bare return, so the pseudo-code shows no work. The facts list forty instructions, which the pseudo-code does not reflect.

name: copy_strided_words_into_table
description: Copies a run of 16-bit words into a global table, stepping the source by four bytes and the table by two. The source address comes from the input when the low bit of a data register is set.

name: silence_audio_channels
description: Clears the DMA enable bits for the four audio channels and sets the volume register of each channel to zero.

name: store_longwords_at_table_offsets
description: Walks a table of offset and value entries and writes each 32-bit value into a second table at the offset given by its entry. The loop count comes from a global value.

name: read_disk_blocks_copy_loader
description: Fills in disk I/O request blocks and calls the I/O routine to read blocks from disk into memory. It then writes interrupt-enable and DMA control words and copies a 4 KB block of loader code to address zero.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data

name: select_drive_and_read_track
description: Selects the disk drive through a CIA port, sets the disk DMA pointer and length, and calls positioning routines. It then scans the track data for the MFM sync pattern. The facts list the disk pointer, disk length and DMA control registers.

key: Blades of Steel (1990)(Novotrade)[cr Paranoimia].adf boot-block load +$800 to $020000 (4096 bytes):0:02A8
name: copy_words_from_offset
description: Copies a run of 16-bit words from a source address offset by a global value into a destination pointer, for a count given in a data register.

key: Blades of Steel (1990)(Novotrade)[cr Paranoimia].adf boot-block load +$800 to $020000 (4096 bytes):0:02C0
name: decode_mfm_sector_bits
description: Decodes MFM-encoded data over ten passes. Each pass extracts the data bits from the odd and even positions of two long-word fields with mask operations and writes the result into a destination buffer with a fixed stride.

key: Blades of Steel (1990)(Novotrade)[cr Paranoimia].adf boot-block load +$800 to $020000 (4096 bytes):0:0334
name: skip_mfm_sync_words
description: Searches forward for the MFM sync word and then skips any consecutive sync words, leaving the pointer at the first non-sync data.

key: Blades of Steel (1990)(Novotrade)[cr Paranoimia].adf boot-block load +$800 to $020000 (4096 bytes):0:034E
name: step_disk_head_to_track
description: Moves a current track counter toward a target one step at a time. It sets the step direction and step bits in a CIA port before each step and calls a routine to wait between steps.

key: Blades of Steel (1990)(Novotrade)[cr Paranoimia].adf boot-block load +$800 to $020000 (4096 bytes):0:03B2
name: wait_for_interrupt_request_bit
description: Busy-waits until one bit of a status word is set, then stores a fixed acknowledge value. The facts list the interrupt request registers as touched.

key: Blades of Steel (1990)(Novotrade)[cr Paranoimia].adf boot-block load +$800 to $020000 (4096 bytes):0:03D0
name: wait_for_cia_status_clear
description: Runs a fixed delay loop, then busy-waits until one status bit of the fire-button port clears.

key: Blades of Steel (1990)(Novotrade)[cr Paranoimia].adf boot-block load +$800 to $020000 (4096 bytes):0:03EC
name: repeat_until_status_bit_clears
description: Repeats a routine while a status bit remains set, setting the low control bits before each call, then clears the status word. It touches the fire-button port and the drive select port.

key: Blades of Steel (1990)(Novotrade)[cr Paranoimia].adf boot-block load +$800 to $020000 (4096 bytes):0:0420
name: wait_for_cia_interrupt_flag
description: Busy-waits until the CIA B interrupt control register reports its flag bit as set.

key: Blades of Steel (1990)(Novotrade)[cr Paranoimia].adf boot-block load +$800 to $020000 (4096 bytes):0:043E
name: pulse_drive_select_bit
description: Sets one bit of a CIA B port chosen from the low two bits of its input, holds it through a fixed delay loop, clears it, then calls a routine and clears a state word.

key: Blades of Steel (1990)(Novotrade)[cr Paranoimia].adf boot-block load +$800 to $020000 (4096 bytes):0:047E
name: pulse_drive_control_bit
description: Sets bit seven and one bit selected by the input's low two bits in a control word, clears the selected bit after a delay loop, and sets the word to all ones.

name: program_blitter_from_block
description: Waits until the blitter is idle, then copies a block of parameters into the blitter registers for source, destination, modulo, control and size.

name: poll_until_high_word_clears
description: Writes a fixed value to a control field, then repeatedly calls a routine and stores its low word until the high word of the returned value is zero. It waits on a status flag in each pass.

name: forward_call_to_routine
description: Calls one routine and returns, adding no logic of its own. The gap bytes decode as this code.

name: copy_table_entry_double_buffers
description: Looks up a three-word entry from a table indexed by a shifted value, optionally replaces the last word with all ones, and writes the three words into two parallel buffers at an offset taken from a stored position.

name: advance_frame_counter_and_call
description: Calls two routines, increments a 16-bit counter in the object, then calls a third routine. The counter is the only data it changes directly.

name: write_longword_pairs_to_buffers
description: Writes a pair of 32-bit values, as high and low words, into two parallel buffers, then writes a second pair eight and twelve bytes further on. The offset comes from the input register.

name: init_sprite_position_from_table
description: Looks up a base value in a table indexed by a short entry, adds a second value from the same entry and stores the sum. It then sets two 16-bit fields to all ones and one to zero.

name: setup_paired_buffer_objects
description: Initializes an object's fields with a size and an offset, computes two buffer addresses at fixed distances, and calls a routine twice to program them. When a table value is not one it also resets a second set of fields.

name: clamp_offset_adjusted_value
description: Subtracts a stored offset from each of two values when the matching bit in a flag word is set. It then forces the first value to a fixed limit when it lies outside a window.

name: write_sprite_control_bytes
description: Computes a start value from an input and writes it and derived bytes into two control buffers. It decrements a counter in a table entry, and when the counter reaches zero it clears two longwords and returns the counter.

name: setup_graphics_operation_fields
description: Initializes a block of fields for a graphics operation, calls routines to compute an address and a size, and combines a shifted value with a constant into a size field before setting a mode field.

name: queue_optional_graphics_operation
description: When one status bit is set, copies a stored address into the object, sets a size field, optionally offsets the address by a fixed amount and calls a routine to finish the operation.

name: conditional_finish_graphics_operation
description: If one bit of a status byte is set, copies the stored address into the object, calls a routine and clears the mode field.

name: write_longword_into_double_buffers
description: Reads a 32-bit value through a pointer table and writes its high and low words into two parallel buffers at an offset computed from a stored position. It then calls two routines.

name: configure_cia_timer_and_interrupts
description: Writes a sequence of constants to the CIA A timer and interrupt control registers and then to the interrupt enable register, with one call. The routine is straight-line code with no loop.

name: advance_timer_and_acknowledge_interrupt
description: When a status bit is set, advances a counter, and when a timer reaches its limit it resets state fields and calls routines to restart the sequence. It writes an acknowledge value to the interrupt request register at the end.

name: stub_return_input_value
description: Returns its stack value unchanged, so it does nothing observable. It is reached only because gap bytes decode as code.

name: swap_buffer_pointer_sets
description: Swaps several pointer and longword fields between two buffer sets, clears a counter and copies a selected pointer into a global value. The facts list the copper pointer and copper jump registers as touched.

name: compute_position_deltas_and_copy
description: Computes the differences between current and previous coordinate fields, copies several fields into their companion fields, and clears a counter.

name: fill_column_cells_with_ff
description: Computes a table address from a pair of 16-bit inputs, calls one routine, then writes all ones to eight bytes spaced 44 bytes apart in the table.

name: update_position_with_bounds
description: Adjusts an x and a y position by direction flags, clamps each to its range, stores a derived offset from the x value, and calls a routine to finish.

name: reset_cell_loop_then_mark
description: Clears a pending flag if set, computes a table index from position values, and calls two routines repeatedly until one returns zero. It then sets a flag and writes all-ones longwords at two table offsets.

name: program_blitter_three_rows
description: Loops three times, waiting for the blitter to be idle each time, and writes the blitter control, mask, modulo, pointer and size registers. The facts list the blitter registers and the DMA control status.

name: program_blitter_three_rows_swapped
description: Loops three times, waiting for the blitter to be idle each time, and writes the blitter control, mask, modulo, pointer and size registers. It writes the two address values in the opposite order from its neighbour.

name: copy_32_byte_cell_planes
description: Copies a 32-byte entry from a table selected by a shifted index into a destination block, writing each byte at offsets that step by a fixed row spacing and by a second plane offset.

name: copy_32_bytes_strided_destination
description: Copies 32 bytes from an input pointer into a destination block, writing each byte at offsets that step by a fixed row spacing and by a second plane offset.

name: write_four_positions_to_lists
description: Writes four 32-bit positions into each of two output lists, each position being a base offset plus a stored value adjusted by a small amount. It then writes a packed nibble value into two further locations.

name: wait_for_flag_then_clear
description: Busy-waits until a state flag becomes nonzero, then clears it.

name: program_blitter_from_table_entry
description: Loads a value from a table selected by its input, waits until the blitter is idle, then writes a set of blitter registers with constants and offsets.

name: copy_32_words_three_destinations
description: Copies 32 words from an input block into three destinations: two state structures and a fixed table in the object.

name: clear_flag_word
description: Sets one 16-bit state word to zero and returns. Its only effect is that clearing.

name: reset_state_fields_to_defaults
description: Sets four longwords to all ones, clears several 16-bit fields in two tables and a state flag, and sets a counter to one. It makes no calls.

name: call_setup_sequence_routines
description: Calls a routine with an argument computed from its input, then calls two more routines. It holds no logic of its own beyond those calls.

name: copy_16_words_then_call
description: Copies sixteen 16-bit words from an input block into a fixed table in the object, then calls one routine on that table.

name: build_rows_from_two_lists
description: When a first counter is nonzero, initializes a set of position fields and calls a routine in a loop, advancing a stored address by a fixed stride each pass until the routine returns zero. It repeats the same loop for a second list when a second counter is nonzero.

name: place_flagged_cells_into_lists
description: Loops over an input list of entries and, for each entry whose flag is negative, computes a position from table values and clamps a vertical value to a window. It writes control words and then calls a routine five times with fixed strides between calls.

description: Writes a fixed value to a control field, then repeatedly calls a routine and stores its low word until the high word of the returned value is zero. It waits on a status flag in each pass.

name: forward_call_to_routine
description: Calls one routine and returns, adding no logic of its own. The gap bytes decode as this code.

name: copy_table_entry_double_buffers
description: Looks up a three-word entry from a table indexed by a shifted value, optionally replaces the last word with all ones, and writes the three words into two parallel buffers at an offset taken from a stored position.

name: advance_frame_counter_and_call
description: Calls two routines, increments a 16-bit counter in the object, then calls a third routine. The counter is the only data it changes directly.

name: write_longword_pairs_to_buffers
description: Writes a pair of 32-bit values, as high and low words, into two parallel buffers, then writes a second pair eight and twelve bytes further on. The offset comes from the input register.

name: init_sprite_position_from_table
description: Looks up a base value in a table indexed by a short entry, adds a second value from the same entry and stores the sum. It then sets two 16-bit fields to all ones and one to zero.

name: setup_paired_buffer_objects
description: Initializes an object's fields with a size and an offset, computes two buffer addresses at fixed distances, and calls a routine twice to program them. When a table value is not one it also resets a second set of fields.

name: clamp_offset_adjusted_value
description: Subtracts a stored offset from each of two values when the matching bit in a flag word is set. It then forces the first value to a fixed limit when it lies outside a window.

name: write_sprite_control_bytes
description: Computes a start value from an input and writes it and derived bytes into two control buffers. It decrements a counter in a table entry, and when the counter reaches zero it clears two longwords and returns the counter.

name: setup_graphics_operation_fields
description: Initializes a block of fields for a graphics operation, calls routines to compute an address and a size, and combines a shifted value with a constant into a size field before setting a mode field.

name: queue_optional_graphics_operation
description: When one status bit is set, copies a stored address into the object, sets a size field, optionally offsets the address by a fixed amount and calls a routine to finish the operation.

name: conditional_finish_graphics_operation
description: If one bit of a status byte is set, copies the stored address into the object, calls a routine and clears the mode field.

name: write_longword_into_double_buffers
description: Reads a 32-bit value through a pointer table and writes its high and low words into two parallel buffers at an offset computed from a stored position. It then calls two routines.

name: configure_cia_timer_and_interrupts
description: Writes a sequence of constants to the CIA A timer and interrupt control registers and then to the interrupt enable register, with one call. The routine is straight-line code with no loop.

name: advance_timer_and_acknowledge_interrupt
description: When a status bit is set, advances a counter, and when a timer reaches its limit it resets state fields and calls routines to restart the sequence. It writes an acknowledge value to the interrupt request register at the end.

name: stub_return_input_value
description: Returns its stack value unchanged, so it does nothing observable. It is reached only because gap bytes decode as code.

name: swap_buffer_pointer_sets
description: Swaps several pointer and longword fields between two buffer sets, clears a counter and copies a selected pointer into a global value. The facts list the copper pointer and copper jump registers as touched.

name: compute_position_deltas_and_copy
description: Computes the differences between current and previous coordinate fields, copies several fields into their companion fields, and clears a counter.

name: fill_column_cells_with_ff
description: Computes a table address from a pair of 16-bit inputs, calls one routine, then writes all ones to eight bytes spaced 44 bytes apart in the table.

name: update_position_with_bounds
description: Adjusts an x and a y position by direction flags, clamps each to its range, stores a derived offset from the x value, and calls a routine to finish.

name: reset_cell_loop_then_mark
description: Clears a pending flag if set, computes a table index from position values, and calls two routines repeatedly until one returns zero. It then sets a flag and writes all-ones longwords at two table offsets.

name: program_blitter_three_rows
description: Loops three times, waiting for the blitter to be idle each time, and writes the blitter control, mask, modulo, pointer and size registers. The facts list the blitter registers and the DMA control status.

name: program_blitter_three_rows_swapped
description: Loops three times, waiting for the blitter to be idle each time, and writes the blitter control, mask, modulo, pointer and size registers. It writes the two address values in the opposite order from its neighbour.

name: copy_32_byte_cell_planes
description: Copies a 32-byte entry from a table selected by a shifted index into a destination block, writing each byte at offsets that step by a fixed row spacing and by a second plane offset.

name: copy_32_bytes_strided_destination
description: Copies 32 bytes from an input pointer into a destination block, writing each byte at offsets that step by a fixed row spacing and by a second plane offset.

name: write_four_positions_to_lists
description: Writes four 32-bit positions into each of two output lists, each position being a base offset plus a stored value adjusted by a small amount. It then writes a packed nibble value into two further locations.

name: wait_for_flag_then_clear
description: Busy-waits until a state flag becomes nonzero, then clears it.

name: program_blitter_from_table_entry
description: Loads a value from a table selected by its input, waits until the blitter is idle, then writes a set of blitter registers with constants and offsets.

name: copy_32_words_three_destinations
description: Copies 32 words from an input block into three destinations: two state structures and a fixed table in the object.

name: clear_flag_word
description: Sets one 16-bit state word to zero and returns. Its only effect is that clearing.

name: reset_state_fields_to_defaults
description: Sets four longwords to all ones, clears several 16-bit fields in two tables and a state flag, and sets a counter to one. It makes no calls.

name: call_setup_sequence_routines
description: Calls a routine with an argument computed from its input, then calls two more routines. It holds no logic of its own beyond those calls.

name: copy_16_words_then_call
description: Copies sixteen 16-bit words from an input block into a fixed table in the object, then calls one routine on that table.

name: build_rows_from_two_lists
description: When a first counter is nonzero, initializes a set of position fields and calls a routine in a loop, advancing a stored address by a fixed stride each pass until the routine returns zero. It repeats the same loop for a second list when a second counter is nonzero.

name: place_flagged_cells_into_lists
description: Loops over an input list of entries and, for each entry whose flag is negative, computes a position from table values and clamps a vertical value to a window. It writes control words and then calls a routine five times with fixed strides between calls.

name: read_disk_blocks_copy_loader
description: Fills in disk I/O request blocks and calls the I/O routine to read blocks from disk into memory. It then writes interrupt-enable and DMA control words and copies a 4 KB block of loader code to address zero.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decoded bytes are not valid instructions: a read-modify-write of a word is followed by bad data. The routine is not usable code.

key: Blades of Steel.adf boot-block load +$800 to $020000 (4096 bytes):0:020A
name: select_drive_and_read_track

key: Blades of Steel.adf boot-block load +$800 to $020000 (4096 bytes):0:02A8
name: copy_words_from_offset
description: Copies a run of 16-bit words from a source address offset by a global value into a destination pointer, for a count given in a data register.

key: Blades of Steel.adf boot-block load +$800 to $020000 (4096 bytes):0:02C0
name: decode_mfm_sector_bits
description: Decodes MFM-encoded data over ten passes. Each pass extracts the data bits from the odd and even positions of two long-word fields with mask operations and writes the result into a destination buffer with a fixed stride.

key: Blades of Steel.adf boot-block load +$800 to $020000 (4096 bytes):0:0334
name: skip_mfm_sync_words
description: Searches forward for the MFM sync word and then skips any consecutive sync words, leaving the pointer at the first non-sync data.

key: Blades of Steel.adf boot-block load +$800 to $020000 (4096 bytes):0:034E
name: step_disk_head_to_track
description: Moves a current track counter toward a target one step at a time. It sets the step direction and step bits in a CIA port before each step and calls a routine to wait between steps.

key: Blades of Steel.adf boot-block load +$800 to $020000 (4096 bytes):0:03B2
name: wait_for_interrupt_request_bit
description: Busy-waits until one bit of a status word is set, then stores a fixed acknowledge value. The facts list the interrupt request registers as touched.

key: Blades of Steel.adf boot-block load +$800 to $020000 (4096 bytes):0:03D0
name: wait_for_cia_status_clear
description: Runs a fixed delay loop, then busy-waits until one status bit of the fire-button port clears.

key: Blades of Steel.adf boot-block load +$800 to $020000 (4096 bytes):0:03EC
name: repeat_until_status_bit_clears
description: Repeats a routine while a status bit remains set, setting the low control bits before each call, then clears the status word. It touches the fire-button port and the drive select port.

key: Blades of Steel.adf boot-block load +$800 to $020000 (4096 bytes):0:0420
name: wait_for_cia_interrupt_flag
description: Busy-waits until the CIA B interrupt control register reports its flag bit as set.

key: Blades of Steel.adf boot-block load +$800 to $020000 (4096 bytes):0:043E
name: pulse_drive_select_bit
description: Sets one bit of a CIA B port chosen from the low two bits of its input, holds it through a fixed delay loop, clears it, then calls a routine and clears a state word.

key: Blades of Steel.adf boot-block load +$800 to $020000 (4096 bytes):0:047E
name: pulse_drive_control_bit
description: Sets bit seven and one bit selected by the input's low two bits in a control word, clears the selected bit after a delay loop, and sets the word to all ones.
